title: Prove shared TypeScript terminal UI in WebView2 and VS Code
starting_commit_note: The supplied workspace is not a Git checkout; authority hashes and the SP00-T03 snapshot are the immutable starting references.

prerequisites.required_output: Repository skeleton, pinned Node/TypeScript/.NET toolchain, and isolated prototype paths

global_invariants: The same compiled TypeScript renderer and canonical fixture are used by both hosts.
Closing either host owns no process, terminal, scheduler, or workflow state.
Terminal output is untrusted presentation data and cannot invoke host commands.
Only one controller mode is shown as CONTROL; observation remains distinct from input authority.
Hidden panes reduce presentation frequency without losing sequence correctness.
Prototype code remains isolated and is not referenced by production projects.

acceptance.result: WebView2 and VS Code report the same canonical fixture hash and equivalent semantic proof outcomes.
Both hosts record render duration and browser memory data for one, four, and eight active xterm.js terminals.
Hidden terminal panes retain every accepted sequence while using the slower hidden render schedule, then catch up after reveal.
Dark, light, high-contrast, 100%, 150%, and 200% fixture states retain accessible terminal and controller names.
Both host bridges reject unknown types and fields; the VS Code webview and WebView2 shell expose no arbitrary command path and enforce local-only content policies.
acceptance.verifier: deterministic contract tests and source validator
acceptance.evidence: test output and source validation log

discretion: Fixture labels, local helper types, and evidence file names may change without changing proof semantics.
The host runner may use an installed VS Code stable or insiders executable, but its exact version must be recorded.
No production layout schema, daemon protocol, process ownership, or workflow authority may be introduced by this proof.
stop_conditions: The two hosts require divergent state or terminal sequence models.
xterm.js cannot preserve bounded output, input focus, or accessible labels in either host.
A strict local-only host policy cannot load the same compiled UI assets.
Hidden-pane throttling requires dropping sequence data.
A required change would reference prototype code from a production project.
expected_outputs: One shared TypeScript/xterm.js workspace loaded by WPF/WebView2 and a VS Code webview
Strict bridge schemas and local-only host policies
Canonical eight-terminal fixture and 27-cell render matrix
Cross-host evidence comparison and fail-closed Windows runner
Source manifest, proof record, validation log, and completion receipt
